messages:
Alex K.: Uploading the pen-test + vuln-scan bundle for ACME's vendor review. Zipped package contains: pen-test report (pdf), Nessus export (nessus.xml), nmap output, remediation-tracker.csv, and per-issue evidence (screenshots/logs). Link: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/artifacts/acme-security-bundle-1785259876.zip
SHA256: 3b7f2a9d6c8e4e2b9d5f8a1c2e6f7a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f

SecurityBot: External scan run complete. Tools: Nessus Professional, nmap 7.93. High-level breakdown: 1 CRITICAL (CVE-2023-XXXX), 5 HIGH, 12 MEDIUM, 7 LOW. CSV "remediation-tracker.csv" includes severity, CVE references, and initial suggested remediation steps. :eyes:

Maria S.: Thanks Alex. Sales needs a per-item owner + ETA column before we send to the customer's security team. Can you map owners and reasonable timelines (ETA as YYYY-MM-DD)? Also the customer asked for signed evidence — is that something we can provide?

Alex K.: Yep — added owner mapping and ETA draft. Quick view pasted below, full CSV updated in the zip.
```
issue_id,short_desc,severity,owner,eta
PT-001,Exposed RDP on bastion,CRITICAL,Kevin L.,2026-03-25
PT-014,Outdated OpenSSL,HIGH,Infra-Team,2026-04-02
PT-022,Missing CSP header,MEDIUM,Web-Platform,2026-03-30
```
I also added per-issue evidence filenames (e.g., PT-001-rdp-screenshot.png, PT-014-openssl-output.txt). For signed evidence we can provide a signed attestation PDF from InfoSec. Who should it be addressed to?

Kevin L.: Quick notes on PT-001 (critical): bastion had RDP (3389) open to 0.0.0.0/0 due to a misapplied terraform rule. Mitigation plan: 1) remove wide rule, 2) enforce SSH bastion + SSM, 3) rotate bastion keypair. Risk window: depends on change window — I can cut the firewall rule and validate config drift within the next 24 hours if approved. ETA 2026-03-25 is conservative to include testing and canary.

Maria S.: Please include the change-request id and on-call contact in the tracker. Customer name for attestation: Acme Corp (security@acme.example). They asked for a short summary and contact for follow-ups. Also they requested confirmation that any customer data was not exposed.

Alex K.: Added change-request link: https://selfservice.redwood-internal/changes/CHG-7821 and on-call for March 24-26 set to kevin@redwood.com. Confirmed: no customer data found in exported evidence. Signed attestation draft added to the zip at /attestation/acme-attestation-2026-03-24.pdf (will sign with InfoSec GPG key and PDF stamp). Updated zip link: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/artifacts/acme-security-bundle-1785259876-v2.zip
New SHA256: a1d4f9b3c7e6d5f2b8c9e0a4f3b2c1d0e9f8a7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4

Kevin L.: I added remediation steps and test checklist to the tracker. For PT-014 (OpenSSL) I included the exact patch command and verification snippet: 
```
# on affected host
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade openssl -y
openssl version -a
# verify no vulnerable CVE string
```
Evidence files updated accordingly.

Maria S.: Perfect. I'll send the bundle to Acme's security team tomorrow morning and note a 48-hour follow-up SLA for any clarifying requests. Sales asked for a one-paragraph customer-facing summary — can someone write that, 2-3 sentences?

Alex K.: Draft for customer-facing summary: "Redwood completed an external penetration test and vulnerability scan for your account. The assessment identified one critical finding which has been scheduled for immediate remediation, along with several high and medium issues; remediation ownership, timelines, and evidence have been supplied in the attached bundle. Attached also is a signed attestation confirming no customer data was exposed." Feel free to tweak.

Maria S.: That's great — I'll send as-is. Thanks all. :+1: If Acme requests deeper evidence we have the raw logs and pcap in the evidence folder; we'll respond within the 48-hour window.

Alex K.: Noted. If anything changes ping me or drop updates in #eng-security. I'll keep the S3 object under versioned path and not delete until legal signs off.

SecurityBot: Reminder — retention policy for security artifacts: 90 days by default. If legal requires longer, please open retention ticket.

Kevin L.: I'll thumbs-up the tracker after a final validation run tonight.

Maria S.: Sending tomorrow 09:00 PT. Closing thread unless further comments.
